published_statement: p.14: 'However, as Deutsch and Candelas [61] showed many years ago, in the neighborhood of a curved surface for conformally invariant theories, <T^{mu nu}> diverges as eps^-3, where eps is the distance from the surface, with a coefficient proportional to the sum of the principal curvatures of the surface. ... For example, for the case of a sphere, the leading surface divergence has the form, for conformal fields, for r = a + eps, eps -> 0, <T^{mu nu}> = (A/eps^3) [2/a 0 0 0; 0 0 0 0; 0 0 a 0; 0 0 0 a sin^2 theta] (58) [as the text layer renders it], in spherical polar coordinates, where the constant is A = 1/720 pi^2 for a scalar field satisfying Dirichlet boundary conditions, or A = 1/60 pi^2 for the electromagnetic field satisfying perfect conductor boundary conditions. Note that (58) is properly traceless. The cubic divergence in the energy density near the surface translates into the quadratic divergence in the energy found for a conducting ball [67]. The corresponding quadratic divergence in the stress corresponds to the absence of the cubic divergence in <T^rr>.' p.15 caution: 'A priori, we do not know which energy-momentum tensor to employ, and the local vacuum-fluctuation energy density is to a large extent meaningless ... the coefficients of the divergent terms depend on the regularization scheme.'
published_hypotheses: H1 conformally invariant field (conformal scalar xi = 1/6, or the Maxwell field)
H2 ideal boundary: Dirichlet for the scalar, PERFECT CONDUCTOR for EM (n x E = 0, n.B = 0)
H3 smooth closed surface; for (58) a sphere of radius a
H4 EXTERIOR point: r = a + eps (the equation is stated for this side only)
H5 leading asymptotic order only, eps -> 0 (eps << a); (57) carries eps^-2, eps^-1 corrections T^(2), T^(1)
H6 flat (Minkowski) background; vacuum expectation value of the renormalised (bulk-subtracted) stress tensor

H7 (Milton's own scope caution, p.15) the local near-surface density is regularisation- and stress-tensor-dependent and 'to a large extent meaningless' except as it couples to gravity (p.3: gravity is 'the exception', 'largely uncharted')

DISCREPANCY (text layer, not a refutation): the alphaXiv text layer renders (58) as diag(2/a, 0, a, a sin^2 theta) contravariant; with g = diag(-1, 1, r^2, r^2 sin^2 theta) that has trace A(a^4(sin^4 theta + 1) - 2)/(a eps^3) != 0, contradicting the adjacent 'properly traceless'. The traceless reading needs T^thth = A/(a^3 eps^3) (orthonormal: u = 2A/(a eps^3), p_t = A/(a eps^3), p_r = 0), which is what the tree and Saharian use (rederive A1-A3). Fractions are lost in this text layer elsewhere too; MUST NOT be quoted as an error in Milton until the typeset PDF glyphs are read.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis for this result: that the authors lacked data. A_EM contains NO measured datum -- it is a number fixed by the Maxwell field and the perfect-conductor boundary condition, and it is re-obtained here from an exact mode sum to 1e-4..1e-5 with nothing borrowed from Milton's (58) or the tree. So no later measurement can move A_EM, and none has: evidence AGAINST the hypothesis for the coefficient itself. What the idealisation lacks is the real conductor's response above omega_p. That was not unknown to the authors -- Milton 1005.0031 eqs. (53)-(55) (citing Sopova-Ford 2005) records that a plasma surface softens the flat-plate divergences, and p.15 calls the local density regularisation-dependent; Saharian states the validity range (a-r)^-1 << omega_0. Having that data does not change A_EM; it changes WHICH term dominates, and the tree already computes that (crossover coefficient K_SF/A_EM = 2.0826, a_c = 0.480 c/omega_p, tolman.py:1517-1527). Where it would bite is the tree's quotation of delta at a femtometre and at l_P (tolman.py:622-625), outside H2's physical range -- a scope limit on those numbers, not a defect in the external result.
grade_evidence: (1) READ at source: Milton 1005.0031 eq. (58) gives A = 1/(60 pi^2) for perfect-conductor EM, stated for the exterior r = a + eps. (2) The tree's INTERIOR use (u = -hbar c/(30 pi^2 a eps^3), p_r = -hbar c/(60 pi^2 a^2 eps^2)) is exactly Saharian 0708.1187 eq. (14.21) (READ), so the side added by the tree is published and true. (3) Machine check independent of both Milton's (58) and the tree: Saharian's exact interior mode sum (14.20), validated at the centre against -0.0381/a^4, extrapolates to (a-r)^3 eps -> -0.0033774 (deg 4; target -1/(30 pi^2) = -0.0033774) and (a-r)^2 p_r -> -0.0016890 (target -0.0016887). (4) Sympy: conservation forces the tree's p_r on both sides; every tree quantity built on A_EM (m, chi, delta limit, crossover 15 sqrt2 pi/32, a_c = 0.480169 skin) re-derives. (5) No datum enters A_EM, so none can have moved it. Drifts recorded, none moving the grade: attribution of the interior to an exterior equation (covered by Saharian); SINGLE-SOURCE status now stale (two sources + computation); ideal-conductor validity range not restated at tolman.py:622-625; text-layer typography of (58) not traceless as rendered (discrepancy, not refutation).
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: if the tree's delta values at a femtometre and at eps = l_P (tolman.py:622-625) are read as physical claims about a real conductor rather than as values of the ideal-conductor closed form -- the result holds only for eps >> c/omega_p (Saharian 0708.1187 p.60), a range the tree does not restate at that site; or if the ruling requires the cited equation itself (Milton (58), exterior) to cover the interior use, since only Saharian (14.21) states the interior. To WRONG: a published or computed interior coefficient differing from 1/(30 pi^2 a) for u -- the exact mode sum here excludes that to ~1e-4. Toward a firmer STANDS: reading Deutsch & Candelas 1979 itself (no arXiv copy), and reading the typeset glyphs of Milton's (58) to settle the text-layer discrepancy.
